features.label: Translation features
features.chatDescription: Your spoken language, translation languages and models stay visible on Home. Click a choice to change it—no settings hunt.
features.chatMute: Pauses capture when your VRChat mic is muted by default; toggle this on Home.
features.chatFinish: Can finish an already-captured sentence after you mute.
features.chatEarly: Choose up to four translation languages; extra languages take more time and chatbox space.
features.subtitlesDescription: Read translated voices in a movable window. This is a separate feature: it is not needed to translate your own microphone.
features.subtitlesCapture: Listen only to VRChat, another chosen application, or all playback.
features.subtitlesLanguage: Choose spoken and subtitle languages. Use FireRedASR2 for Chinese/English or a multilingual recognizer.
features.subtitlesSpeakers: Optional AI voice identification attaches speaker names to subtitles.
speakers.title: Follow other people’s voices
speakers.description: Start subtitles separately when you want them. Optional local AI compares voices—not where people stand—to suggest who is speaking.
speakers.identifyDescription: Shows “Maybe…” with ✓/✕ instead of assuming who is speaking. Subtitles don’t wait for confirmation. Turning recognition off unloads its model while translation continues.
speakers.namesDescription: Save names and photos, review suggestions and see confirmed/rejected counts. Only clear, reviewed voice examples improve matching; guesses never teach themselves. Everything stays on your device.
speakers.note: Saved voice examples help with names, not with separating voices. Optional Groups mode uses local VibeVoice to try to recognize overlapping speech. It adds delay and uses more memory, and can still make mistakes.
setup.title: From install to your first message
setup.description: Setup prepares your own voice translation first. Subtitles, People and Groups can wait until you want them.
setup.installDescription: Run the installer and choose Just me or All users. Leave Open SayWhat? checked to continue into setup.
setup.modelsDescription: Keep the recommendation or choose another model card. Select Prepare translation and follow the download progress. Models run on your PC, not a cloud service.
setup.startDescription: Enable OSC in VRChat, then press Start on Home. Setup does not start listening on its own. Help in the app explains the VRChat connection if you need it.
setup.note: The app interface supports English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean. Interface language is separate from your translation languages.
requirements.title: System requirements
requirements.description: Translation and VRChat share your GPU. Larger models use more memory and may increase delay.
requirements.windowsDescription: Your voice to VRChat chat: Windows 10 build 19044+ or Windows 11. App-only subtitles require Windows 11; on Windows 10, explicitly choose All playback, which includes other apps. Windows 10 compatibility is a preview and has not been verified on a Windows 10 PC.
requirements.speechDescription: Setup prepares the speech tools for your selected mode. Optional subtitle or legacy engines may need Windows virtualization, permission or a restart; the app guides you.
requirements.gpuDescription: Setup checks the available hardware. Speech recognition and translation need memory alongside VRChat; support and speed vary by model and GPU.
requirements.storageDescription: The smaller Hy-MT2 translator is about 1.1 GB. Speech models and tools need additional space; setup shows downloads before preparing them.
requirements.notice: Preview status: hardware compatibility, fresh-PC installation and long VRChat sessions are still being tested. A particular frame rate or translation delay is not guaranteed.
models.title: Choose a model without digging into settings
models.description: Home shows the speech recognizer and translator in use. Click to compare model cards, read what each does and download or switch. A larger model is not automatically better.
models.small: About 1.1 GB for Q4_K_M. Lower memory use leaves more GPU resources for VRChat.
models.large: About 4.6 GB for Q4_K_M. An alternative for comparing translation quality, with higher memory use.
models.gemma: About 2.5 GB. An alternative translator requiring a chosen spoken language and the built-in runtime. Gemma terms apply; the GGUF is a third-party conversion.
models.liquid: About 229 MB for Q4_K_M. Other language pairs are blocked in the app. LFM Open License terms apply.
models.note: Use one shared translator, or choose separate models for your voice and subtitles in Advanced. Loading two models costs additional memory. Models have their own licenses and are downloaded from their listed third-party sources.
privacy.title: Voice processing stays on your PC.
privacy.local: The local workflow does not upload your speech for recognition or translation. Saved people and voice fingerprints remain on your device; recognition is optional.
privacy.downloads: Setup downloads models and tools from third-party providers. Those providers receive normal download connection information, not microphone recordings.
privacy.logs: Logs can contain spoken or translated text. Review them before exporting or posting them for support.
privacy.website: This website has no analytics scripts or tracking cookies. Choosing a website language saves only that preference in a functional cookie for one year; automatic language detection does not save a cookie. Hosting and download services may still receive normal request metadata.
help.title: Help
faq.separateQuestion: Do I need LM Studio or FoxTrans separately?
faq.separateAnswer: No separate translation app is required for the automatic setup. SayWhat? includes its capture host and translator runtime, then prepares speech support and downloads models after you approve setup. Existing compatible installations can be reused from Advanced.
faq.multipleQuestion: Can my voice translate into several languages?
faq.multipleAnswer: Yes. Choose one to four output languages on Home. Translations share one chat message and one loaded translator. Extra languages take more time and share VRChat’s 144-character space, so long messages may be shortened. The app shows a quiet reminder. Your selected model must support all chosen languages.
faq.changingQuestion: Will translated messages keep changing while I speak?
faq.changingAnswer: Optional early messages are cumulative translations of the sentence so far. They are submitted chat bubbles, not keyboard drafts. The recognizer keeps the entire utterance as context and the completed sentence supplies the definitive translation. Updates are coalesced to roughly 1.5 seconds or slower; chatbox text is limited to 144 characters and 9 displayed lines. Long messages show a readable tail, not the whole paragraph at once.
faq.overlapQuestion: Can it separate people who talk at the same time?
faq.overlapAnswer: Optional Groups mode (experimental) uses local VibeVoice to try to recognize what each person says and show separate translated messages. It adds delay and uses more memory. It does not create isolated audio or guarantee that overlapping speech is understood. Saved voice examples help with names, not with separating voices.
faq.delayQuestion: Why is translation slow on a powerful PC?
faq.delayAnswer: Delay includes the pause after speech, recognition finishing, translation and the chatbox send cadence. VRChat and local models also share GPU resources. Try the smaller translator, one shared model, or just one translation direction. Advanced has timing and troubleshooting information; a larger model alone does not solve every delay.
faq.closeQuestion: What happens when I close the app?
faq.closeAnswer: SayWhat? asks whether to quit and release its model memory or keep running in the system tray. You can remember your choice and change it later in Settings. Closing the subtitle window stops subtitles independently.
faq.updateQuestion: Can I update or uninstall without losing models?
faq.updateAnswer: The app checks for updates on launch unless you turn this off. Choose Update now to download and verify the installer, install with visible progress and reopen the app with translation stopped. Settings and models are kept. Windows may still ask for permission; safety errors remain visible. Manual setup offers update, repair and uninstall with optional data choices.
faq.oscQuestion: How do I enable OSC in VRChat?
faq.oscAnswer: Open VRChat’s Action Menu and select OSC → Enabled. SayWhat?'s sidebar checks local OSC availability and offers guidance if it cannot verify a connection. This is not a chat-delivery acknowledgment: chatbox visibility and user safety settings can still affect what other people see. See VRChat’s official OSC guide for current instructions.
faq.problemQuestion: Where do I report a problem?
faq.problemAnswer: Open Advanced → Diagnostics in the app. Note which direction stopped, your selected models and the timing shown, then report the problem on GitHub. Review logs for private conversation text before sharing them.

setup.languagesDescription: Choose your spoken language and one to four translation languages. You can change them again directly on Home.
models.roles: The speech recognizer turns your voice into words. The translator turns those words into your chosen languages. You can choose each separately.
faq.sourceQuestion: Why choose the language I speak?
faq.sourceAnswer: Giving the recognizer your spoken language can reduce language mix-ups. Automatic is available if you switch languages often. A selected model may support only certain languages; the app explains those limits before you change it.
models.nativeSpeech: Runs directly on Windows. Your spoken-language choice can guide recognition. The app prepares the local tools and model; no separate speech app to open.
models.legacySpeech: The existing real-time speech option. Uses app-managed Ubuntu/WSL tools and automatic language detection. Available for compatible existing setups and subtitle workflows.
